column5: An obligation would make the instalments unknown
column6: It protects the card network from the issuer's discount claims
column7: Discounts on financing instalments are always prohibited
column8: Lowering instalments is riba, since it changes the price
column10: Basis 6/2(b): an obligation would make the instalments (the consideration) unknown; it keeps discounts at the issuer's choice without custom.

column4: Ahmad deposits an amount with Bank A specifically for a card he uses only up to that deposited balance. Which card type is this?
column5: Debit Card
column6: Credit Card
column7: Prepaid Card
column8: Charge Card
column10: Per 3/2/1, in a Prepaid Card the cardholder deposits with the issuer a balance specifically for the card; it is a settlement, not credit, instrument.

column4: Why does a conversion into the card's currency at the merchant's point of sale need not be limited to actual cost, even on a lending-based card?
column5: The merchant bears the exchange risk
column6: It is done by an entity separate from the card issuer
column7: The cardholder pays it in cash at the point of sale
column8: Currency exchange is never limited to cost under any card
column10: Basis 5/5/2: the exchange is by an entity separate from the issuer, so there is no objection of a loan combined with the exchange service.

column4: Bank A, an Institution, issues charge cards. Ahmad delays settling his balance beyond the specified period. May Bank A stipulate interest on the delay?
column5: Yes, at a rate below the market rate
column6: Yes, as pre-agreed in the card terms
column7: Yes, once the grace period has lapsed
column8: No, that would lead to lending on interest
column10: Per 4/3/1 (and 3/3/4), dealing with a charge card must not lead to lending on interest, including stipulating interest if the holder delays.

column4: Bank A wants to join an international card network whose rules include interest on lending. What is the ruling?
column5: Permitted, provided Bank A avoids those violations
column6: Permitted only for debit cards with no fees
column7: Not permitted under any circumstances, even if rules are avoided
column8: Permitted, accepting all the network's terms as they stand
column10: Per 5/3/1, Institutions may join card networks provided they avoid any Shari'ah violations stipulated, such as interest or penalty on lending.

column4: Ahmad cancels his card. Bank A cannot recover the prepaid service cost from the actual provider or reassign it. When may Bank A keep those fees?
column5: Only if Ahmad used the card at least once
column6: Always, whatever the agreement says, as the fee is earned
column7: If this was stated in the card issuance agreement
column8: Never; unused service fees are always refunded to the holder
column10: Per 5/2/4, if the issuer cannot retrieve the cost or reassign the service, it may not return the fees, provided this is stated in the agreement.

column4: Ahmad holds a charge card and asks to pay this month's purchases in instalments over a year. What does the card arrangement provide?
column5: Instalments over a year if he pays a fixed monthly fee
column6: Instalments over a year, with profit added to the balance
column7: Instalments over a year at no extra cost if he asks the issuer
column8: No revolving credit; settlement is within the set period
column10: Per 3/3/3, the charge card does not provide revolving credit (instalments); the holder must settle within the specified period.

column4: Bank A cancels Ahmad's card because he kept using it for Shari'ah-prohibited purchases. How is the treatment of the fees determined?
column5: All fees are doubled as a penalty for the prohibited usage
column6: As if Ahmad himself requested the cancellation
column7: As a cancellation not caused by Ahmad, so fees are returned pro rata
column8: All fees are refunded in full, since Bank A cancelled
column10: Per 5/2/5, cancellation by the issuer for a valid Shari'ah reason attributed to the holder follows the ruling of cancellation at his request.

column4: For a lending-based credit card, which fee must not exceed the actual direct cost?
column5: The subscription fee paid by the issuer to the network
column6: The fee the acquirer charges the card acceptor
column7: An ATM fee charged to other banks' cardholders
column8: The fee for converting used amounts into instalments
column10: Per 5/1/1, fees linked to the loan, incl. converting used amounts into instalments, are capped at actual direct cost; the others fall under 5/1/2.

column4: Ahmad uses his charge card at a store, and Bank A pays the store from its own funds. What is the amount Bank A paid?
column5: An investment by Bank A in the goods
column6: A debt to be claimed from Ahmad
column7: A liability of the store to Bank A
column8: A gift from Bank A to Ahmad
column10: Per 2/2/1/2, if the issuer pays the acceptor from its own funds, the paid amount is a debt to be claimed from the cardholder.

column4: What is the Shari'ah basis for prohibiting revolving credit cards as conventionally structured?
column5: They are a sale of debt for debt between issuer and merchant
column6: They involve gharar in the card limit set by the issuer
column7: They give a revolving loan against a riba-based increment
column8: They involve a prohibited form of Tawarruq
column10: Basis 4/4: the contract gives a revolving loan over time against a riba-based increment, prohibited by Quran, Sunnah, consensus and reason.

column4: Bank A argues that a credit card issuance fee above actual cost is just a service fee. Why does the Shari'ah basis reject this?
column5: It is an artifice for a loan that carries benefit
column6: The fee is unknown to the holder and so it is gharar
column7: The fee is a form of gambling on the cardholder's usage
column8: Service fees are always prohibited when charged by a lender
column10: Basis 5/1/1: an increase over actual direct cost is an artifice to charge an increase over the loan, i.e., a loan carrying benefit for the lender.

column4: Ahmad returns goods bought by card because of a defect that the seller knew about and concealed. Who bears the fees and exchange differences?
column5: The card network bears them
column6: Ahmad may claim them from the seller
column7: Ahmad bears them, with no recourse
column8: Bank A bears them as the issuer
column10: Per 5/7, the holder may not revert to the acceptor for such fees or differences unless the acceptor knew about the defect and concealed it.

column4: Bank A charges a replacement fee on its prepaid card that exceeds the actual cost of replacement. The card involves no lending. What is the ruling?
column5: Permitted only if half is refunded
column6: Not permitted above the actual direct cost
column7: Permitted, as such fees follow the agreement
column8: Not permitted on any prepaid card
column10: Per 5/1/2/3, fees in cards that involve no lending (issuance, renewal, replacement, etc.) are not restricted to actual cost.

column4: Bank A designs a card: it lends Ahmad interest-free, then at due date has him settle the loan via Tawarruq from Bank A, leaving a larger debt. What is the ruling?
column5: Not permitted, as a rollover of the debt
column6: Permitted, as Tawarruq is via Murabahah
column7: Permitted if the profit is modest
column8: Permitted if Bank A acts as agent
column10: Per 6/3/2, a card based on lending then rollover (qalb al-dayn) via Tawarruq, resulting in a debt more than the loan, is not permitted.

column4: Why may a card issuer charge Ahmad the exchange rate difference when he returns goods bought by card, per the jurists' view cited?
column5: The merchant is never liable for defects in goods sold by card
column6: The issuer is the seller of the goods bought by the card
column7: Return costs are a penalty imposed on the buyer by the issuer
column8: The buyer bears the cost of returning the goods
column10: Basis 5/7: jurists held the buyer bears the return burden, as his possession is liability-based and the right to return is his.

column4: Bank A cancels Ahmad's card mid-term due to a restructuring of its card products, with no fault from Ahmad. What applies to the fees?
column5: Bank A keeps all the fees already paid, as the card was issued
column6: Bank A keeps the fees for a year
column7: Bank A returns issuance and service fees pro rata
column8: Bank A returns only the issuance fee and keeps the service fees
column10: Per 5/2/5, if cancellation is for a reason not attributed to the cardholder, the issuer returns issuance and service fees pro rata for the remaining period.

column4: At check-in, a hotel blocks an amount on Ahmad's card to secure what he may owe at check-out. How is the issuer-cardholder relationship characterized here?
column5: Guarantee
column6: Agency for recovery
column7: Novation
column8: Provision of services
column10: Per 2/2/1/2, the relationship is of guarantee if the card is used to block or deduct an amount to secure what will be outstanding on the cardholder.

column4: Bank A plans to offer cardholders free conventional life insurance as a card benefit. What is the ruling?
column5: Permitted for premium cards only, with a separate premium
column6: Not permitted, as it is a prohibited benefit
column7: Permitted, as it is offered for free by the insurer to holders
column8: Permitted if cardholders consent
column10: Per 5/6/1, the issuer may not provide benefits prohibited by Shari'ah, such as conventional life insurance or free access to prohibited places.

column4: With Ahmad's consent, Bank A obtains additional Islamic insurance (Takaful) for his benefit, deducts the contribution and adds a commission. Is this permitted?
column5: No, insurance may not be linked to cards
column6: No, Bank A may not earn a commission
column7: Yes, but only if Bank A pays the contribution
column8: Yes, with or without a commission for Bank A
column10: Per 5/6/3, with the holder's consent, the Institution may obtain additional Islamic insurance for him and deduct the contribution, with or without commission.

column4: At a shop, Ahmad has 1,000 entered on the POS terminal for his card, but receives only 950 in cash in the card's currency. What is the ruling?
column5: Permitted, if the card is a debit card
column6: Not permitted
column7: Permitted, if Ahmad agrees beforehand
column8: Permitted, as the 50 is a service fee
column10: Per 5/8/2, using the card at an acceptor to get cash in the card currency less than the amount entered on the POS is not permitted.

column4: Bank A financed the cover of Ahmad's covered card and lowered one financing instalment because he used little of the cover. What should the agreement state?
column5: Bank A must lower every future instalment
column6: Lowering instalments is never permitted
column7: Bank A is not obliged to lower or repeat it
column8: Bank A must lower it whenever cover is unused
column10: Per 6/2/2/1(b), it must be stated that the issuer is not obliged to lower instalments, and if it lowers one, it need not repeat that later.
